Summary: OpenSSL versions 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, and 3.3 are vulnerable to a Denial of Service (DoS) attack due to excessive memory allocation during TLS 1.3 certificate compression. This issue arises when a peer-supplied uncompressed certificate length from a CompressedCertificate message is used to allocate a heap buffer prior to decompression without being constrained by the max_cert_list setting. This vulnerability affects builds with TLS 1.3 certificate compression enabled and at least one compression algorithm available (brotli, zlib, or zstd). Both clients receiving server CompressedCertificate messages and servers in mutual TLS scenarios receiving client CompressedCertificate messages are impacted. Impact: An attacker can exploit this vulnerability to cause per-connection memory allocations of up to approximately 22 MiB, leading to service degradation or resource exhaustion, potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS). AdditionalInformation: This issue does not result in memory corruption or information disclosure. Servers that do not request client certificates are not vulnerable to client-initiated attacks. OpenSSL versions 3.0, 1.1.1, and 1.0.2 are not affected. The FIPS modules in OpenSSL versions 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, and 3.3 are not impacted as the TLS implementation is outside the OpenSSL FIPS module boundary. Remediation: Apply the latest patches and updates provided by the respective vendors. [Generated by AI]
